title: RTX 4090 idle P-states: new sessions after idle prefill 2.5-3x slower, and the RTX 5090's keep-warm spin (3.5 ms of every 10 ms) does not hold the card in P2
question: Does the RTX 4090 native lane slow new sessions that arrive after idle, as the RTX 5090 did (EXP-060), and does ninfer-serve --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 (EXP-062, shipped for the RTX 5090 in v0.8.2) bring them back to back-to-back speed on this card with identical outputs?

exploratory_observation_before_this_rule.disclosure: Observed before the decision rule below was written; it motivated the experiment and is not counted by the rule.
exploratory_observation_before_this_rule.subject: published v0.6.8-qwen38-4090-beta.1 (binary 32905865, source 5a774841), managed start on the RTX 4090 host, 2026-09-27 14:33-14:37Z
exploratory_observation_before_this_rule.workload: one cold request whose system message (synthetic text plus inert tool JSON, 15,167 prompt tokens) forms the stable prefix, then ten new two-message sessions of 99-103 computed tokens after gaps 0,12,0,30,0,12,0,60,0,45 s; greedy, thinking off, 64 output tokens; nvidia-smi every 50 ms
exploratory_observation_before_this_rule.result: Back to back: prefill 0.146-0.147 s (TTFT 0.170-0.177 s) in P2. After 12-60 s idle every session started in P8 (210 MHz SM, 405 MHz memory) and prefilled in 0.361-0.460 s (TTFT 0.438-0.486 s). The card stepped P2 -> P3 at about 2.3 s, P5 at 3.3-4.3 s and P8 at 5.3-6.3 s after the last response.

decision_rule.arms: One sm_89 ninfer-serve built from alphastorm/ninfer 9d1ef748, launched directly on the RTX 4090 host with the RTX 4090 lane's serving arguments: OFF without --gpu-keep-warm-ms, then ON with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000.
decision_rule.workload_per_arm: One cold request that builds the stable prefix, then 30 new two-message sessions after gaps 0,12,0,25,0,38,0,53,0,58 s repeated three times (15 back to back, three at each of five delays); greedy, thinking off, 64 output tokens, identical prompts in both arms; nvidia-smi every 50 ms. Latency is the server's own prefill time from its request log.
decision_rule.regression: The OFF arm regresses if, at three or more of the five delays, its median prefill is at least 25% and at least 75 ms above its back-to-back median.
decision_rule.recovery: The ON arm recovers if, at every delay, its median prefill is within 10% and within 20 ms of its back-to-back median, and every session after a gap starts in P2.
decision_rule.safety: All 31 responses are byte-identical between the arms, no request fails, and the ON arm's back-to-back median prefill is at most 10% above the OFF arm's.
decision_rule.decision: If regression, recovery and safety all hold, the RTX 4090 profile ships engine.gpu_keep_warm_ms = 60000; otherwise it ships 0. No other grace is chosen from this data.
decision_rule.informational: Power while held (ON arm gaps) against idle (OFF arm gaps); not a gate.

pre_registration.note: The decision rule below was committed and pushed before either arm ran; the exploratory observation was disclosed with it.

answer: The RTX 4090 native lane regresses exactly as the RTX 5090 did, and more: after the last response the card steps P2 -> P3 at about 2.3 s, P5 at 3.3-4.3 s and P8 (210 MHz SM, 405 MHz memory) at 5.4-6.2 s, and every new session after 12-58 s idle started in P8 and prefilled in 0.29-0.47 s against 0.146 s back to back (medians +225 to +288 ms, +153% to +197%). The engine keep-warm that holds the RTX 5090 in P1 does not hold this card: with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 the spin ran (34.9% mean GPU utilization in the gaps) but the card still reached P8, 9.0-10.2 s after the last response instead of 5.4-6.2 s, and every session after a gap again started in P8 (medians 0.355-0.442 s). Outputs were byte-identical between the arms (31 of 31) and back-to-back requests lost nothing (median 0.1463 s against 0.1464 s).
decision: Rule outcome: regression holds at 5 of 5 delays; recovery fails at every delay; safety holds. Under the pre-registered rule the RTX 4090 profile ships engine.gpu_keep_warm_ms = 0 for this spin pattern. An exploratory duty sweep after the rule decided (not counted by it) found what does hold P2 on this card: a single-warp spin of 40 ms or more every 100 ms, while spins of 3.5-6 ms every 10 ms do not. That pattern is a new candidate with its own pre-registered experiment (EXP-066); this receipt does not choose it.

method.host: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (VBIOS 95.02.3c.c0.f4, 450 W limit), Windows 11, driver 610.88, CUDA 13.3; the lane's managed release stopped for the window and left stopped afterwards
method.build: alphastorm/ninfer 9d1ef748 (the v0.8.3 RTX 5090 source; the RTX 4090 kernels equal v0.6.8's 5a774841, and the Q5 tensor-core route is compiled out for sm_89), Release, sm_89, MSVC 14.44 and nvcc 13.3 through the port-native builder tree; ninfer-serve 493fffea
method.arms: The same binary launched directly (outside the managed controller, detached from the SSH session through WMI) with the RTX 4090 lane's v0.6.8 serving arguments on 127.0.0.1:18082: 131,072 context and KV capacity, INT8 KV, prefill chunk 2,048, 2 device-state and 24 host-state slots, 11,264 MiB host KV, 8 private continuations, MTP 3 with the LM-head draft, preserved thinking, a scratch checkpoint root. OFF without --gpu-keep-warm-ms (14:50:59-15:01:47Z), then ON with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 (15:02:04-15:13:00Z).
method.workload: Per arm one cold request whose system message (synthetic text plus inert tool JSON from scripts/agent_mix_probe.py, 15,167 prompt tokens) forms the stable prefix, then 30 new two-message sessions of 97-103 computed tokens after gaps 0,12,0,25,0,38,0,53,0,58 s repeated three times; greedy, thinking off, 64 output tokens; identical prompts in both arms; client through an SSH tunnel, latency from the server's own request log (prefill and TTFT).
method.sampling: nvidia-smi on the host every 50 ms: P-state, SM and memory clocks, power, utilization.

power.note: Means of nvidia-smi samples at under 60% utilization in each state; the ON arm's gaps averaged 23.0 W against 17.9 W for OFF because the spin delayed the step-down, not because it held P2.

exploratory_duty_sweep.disclosure: Run after the rule decided this experiment; not counted by it.
exploratory_duty_sweep.method: A standalone sm_89 program (nvcc 13.3) ran a 3 s full-GPU burst, then a single-warp %globaltimer spin of on_ms every period_ms for 30 s, one pattern at a time with 12 s rests, nothing else on the GPU; nvidia-smi every 50 ms; the last 20 s of each pattern summarized. Host sleeps use the Windows timer, so short periods run longer than nominal and their effective duty is lower (see measured utilization).
exploratory_duty_sweep.reading: Every spin of 40 ms or more every 100 ms held P2 for the whole 30 s at 73-79 W (4.5 W idle in P8); 30 ms every 100 ms did not. Spins of 4-7 ms every 10-20 ms reached P8 even at 60% nominal duty (39.6% measured utilization), so on this card and driver the pattern's period matters, not only its average utilization.

limits: One card, one driver, one Windows host; the RTX 4090's P-state policy may differ under another driver or with a display attached.
Arms ran OFF then ON, not interleaved; the effect sizes (+225 ms and more at every delay, and no recovery at any) are far outside order effects.
Workload prompts are synthetic and short (about 100 computed tokens on a 15K-token prefix); production agent turns are larger, so absolute times differ.
The client ran from the Mac through an SSH tunnel; the numbers are the server's own prefill and TTFT, which exclude the tunnel.
The exploratory duty sweep used a standalone program, not ninfer-serve; EXP-066 measures the chosen pattern inside the engine.
